name: Ivan Ruchkin
title: Malachowsky Family Endowed Rising Star Assistant Professor; TEA Lab Director
department: Electrical and Computer Engineering; affiliate MAE and CISE
fitReason: Direct connection between neural closed-loop control on a current physical racing platform and research on reliable world models, safety prediction and verification.

physicalEvidence.summary: May 8, 2026 TEACar revision evaluates the lab’s physical 1/14-scale prototype with Jetson Orin NX, IMX219 camera and ROS2. Three CNNs trained on 10,000 image/steering pairs from human-driven laps generate steering commands on the vehicle; each controller is operated continuously for 30 minutes, with latency and power measurements. This is learned steering on hardware, not merely a platform proposal. The paper is primarily a systems evaluation; it does not establish deployment of every separate world-model safety method on that car.

shortVisit.summary: Current TEA page restricts its volunteer-research call to UF undergraduate and graduate students and welcomes PhD applications. The PI’s generic research-interest form does not establish an external short-visit opening.

scoreReasons.fit: Neural physical control with direct safe-autonomy and world-model research, albeit the hardware paper’s CNNs are basic learned steering.
scoreReasons.physical: Named 2026 local prototype and explicit closed-loop controller operation by the TEA lab.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Local UF volunteer recruitment and PhD applications only; external master’s route unknown.
scoreReasons.freshness: May 2026 full technical revision, September 2026 lab news and current official faculty affiliation.

name: Mark R. Cutkosky
title: Fletcher Jones Professor; Biomimetics and Dexterous Manipulation Lab faculty
fitReason: Fresh learning-for-contact work complements extensive physical tactile and manipulation research, particularly expanding pretrained visuomotor policies with force information.

physicalEvidence.summary: MuSe, submitted June 29 and revised July 5, 2026, deploys force-aware continual-learning policies on a UR5e with WSG50 gripper, CoinFT sensors and wrist iPhone. The learned model predicts actions and force trajectories for adaptive compliance; actual tasks include wiping, insertion and pick-and-place. Deployment details distinguish 5 Hz RGB, 20 Hz action/proprioception and 120 Hz force streams. This is collaborative work with Shuran Song’s group and includes Cutkosky advisee Seongheon Hong; exact ownership of the shared UR5e is not established.

shortVisit.summary: A still-linked research-position page is expressly for academic year 2024–25 and was last modified May 16, 2025. It mentions local MS course-credit projects, undergraduate Stanford programs, and industrial affiliates. It says students outside Stanford-supported programs are generally difficult to accept and explicitly normally excludes non-program high-school/external undergraduate interns. No current external-master’s short-visit invitation is established.

scoreReasons.fit: Strong direct multimodal policy learning and physical contact manipulation.
scoreReasons.physical: Current named real UR5e deployment, but collaborative hardware with no confirmed independent-lab ownership/access.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Dated 2024–25 recruitment does not invite external master’s short visits; program prerequisites and restrictions remain relevant.
scoreReasons.freshness: July 2026 primary revision, June 2026 BDML page update and current Stanford faculty/advisee record.
